item.title: AmiciMusic: The Sound of America — Thu Nov 12 — Asheville Art Museum
item.description:
Thursday, November 12, 2026 | 7:00 pm – 9:00 pm | $22 for Members; $25 for non-members; $12 for students Event Details and Tickets AmiciMusic returns with a thrilling program entitled “THE SOUND of AMERICA.” Pianist and Artistic Director Daniel Weiser will be joined by violinist Tim Schwarz from Philadelphia in this exciting exploration of the incredible diversity of our American sound.
The program includes Spirituals and Ragtime as well as Blues-inspired works by W.C. Handy and William Grant Still, the Native-American inspirations of Charles Cadman, the Jewish influence on Ernest Bloch, the country fiddling in Aaron Copland, and the Latin rhythms in Bernstein’s West Side Story.
Weiser and Schwarz served as the 1996 U.S. Artistic Ambassadors of Music for which they performed over 50 concerts in 11 countries in the Middle East and Southeast Asia showcasing our American music

item.title: Bluegrass and BBQ ft. The JackTown Ramblers — Thu Nov 12, 5:00 PM — The Farm – A Gathering Place

item.title: The Body of the Golem: A Life in Portraiture — Sun Nov 15, 2:00 PM
item.description:
Artist and writer Riva Lehrer brings together portraiture, Jewish tradition, disability, and the figure of the golem for the 2026 Phyllis Freed Sollod Memorial Lecture in the Mountain View Room of the Sherrill Center. Through art and storytelling, Lehrer explores who gets labeled “monstrous,” who has the power to define that label, and what becomes possible when people claim their own bodies and identities. item.title: Why Your Resolutions Fail by February (and How to Make This Year Different) — Tue Dec 8, 6:00 PM
item.description:
AVL Digital Nomads Every January we set big intentions, and by February most of them have quietly disappeared. It’s rarely about willpower. Usually two things get in the way: practical obstacles we haven’t planned for, and beliefs running underneath that pull us back to the old pattern.
In this 2-hour evening workshop, you’ll design the year you want and then take apart what’s been stopping you, at both levels.
**What we’ll do together:**
* Take a guided meditation into your ideal life, to get clear on what you really want. * Map your goals across the six key areas of life * Pick one goal and identify its practical obstacles, then turn them into simple, doable next steps * Uncover any beliefs holding you back from your goal and keeping you stuck. * Learn neuroplasticity-based tools you can use on your own to start rewiring that belief keeping you stuck.
You’ll leave with a clear goal, a realistic set of the first few baby steps and a worksheet to keep using all year.

item.title: Walking the NC Arboretum at the Willow Pond & Old Mill Trail — Sat Dec 12, 12:00 PM
item.description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group Meet inside the Baker Visitor Center. Restrooms are available at the start point. We will start walking as soon as everyone has arrived.
The walk is a guided 5 KM trail. There are some moderate hills and stair climbing. A significant part of the route is on well-groomed trails with very few obstacles. Some people will want walking poles.
After exploring the Formal Gardens (Winter Lights will be up!), we will walk down Running Cedar Road and turn left on Bent Creek Road. We'll turn right on the Old Mill Trail and go out and back. Then we will take the Wesley Branch Trail and go right on the Lower Willow Pond Trail. After exploring the Willow Pond, we will follow the Upper Willow Pond Trail to the parking lot.
Dress for the weather; consider a hat and sunscreen (yes, even in December). Sneakers should be fine, unless it has rained recently. Be sure to bring **plenty of water** and a protein snack.

item.title: OLD-TIME JAM — Wed Dec 30, 5:00 PM
item.description:
The roots of Appalachian old-time music stretch far across the Atlantic and we're proud to honor and showcase that legacy at Jack of the Wood Pub with our long-running Old-Time Jam sessions — every Wednesday starting at 5pm! Recently recommended by Rolling Stone for "those looking for an organic, participatory [music] experience" in Asheville, the Old-Time Jam is one of several weekly traditional jam sessions hosted at JACK.
Our cozy Celtic pub is the perfect spot downtown to take in some of the region's finest traditional acoustic musicians playing "in the round" while you enjoy a pint or two and the best pub fare in town!
